name: Skate 3
post_apply_message:
Skate 3 (mchughalex/skate3recomp — a static RECOMPILATION of the Xbox 360 build, not an emulator) — Apply points the existing Steam shortcut at the WINDOWS build under GE-Proton 10.34 and turns on portable mode.

WHY THE WINDOWS BUILD ON LINUX: the project's own README says the Windows build 'may have a better experience running through a translation layer like Proton rather than the native Linux build itself' on some hardware, and Tony measured exactly that. The shortcut previously pointed at Skate3Recomp-Linux/skate3; this recipe repoints the SAME appid (3283182477) at Skate3Recomp-Windows/skate3.exe, so your artwork stays put and no duplicate entry appears.

SET THE GRAPHICS API TO VULKAN — this is the single biggest win and it CANNOT be scripted; there's no command-line flag for it. Go to Settings > Video > Graphics API, choose Vulkan, then Apply & Restart. DirectX 12 is the default, and under Proton that means game -> VKD3D-Proton -> Vulkan. Picking Vulkan makes it game -> winevulkan -> Vulkan and drops a whole translation layer.

PORTABLE MODE: the recipe drops an empty portable.txt beside skate3.exe, which the README says keeps all user data in the executable's folder. Without it a Proton run writes saves to %APPDATA%\skate3 INSIDE THE PREFIX, where a prefix wipe destroys them and GFM's save capture can't see them. With it, saves sit in the game folder, travel with Deploy and survive a reimage. NOTE: your progress from the native Linux build lives in the Linux user-data folder and will NOT carry over — copy it in by hand if you want it.

CONTROLLER: Xbox controls are the project's primary input and the Deck/Go 2 present as an Xbox pad, so nothing to do. A PlayStation or Switch pad needs Settings > Controls > Controller Backend = SDL, then a restart (the Linux build always uses SDL; the Windows build under Proton does not).

DLC IS ALREADY INCLUDED — four packs ship in the staged copy and travel with Deploy: Danny's Hawaiian Dream, Maloof Money Cup 2010 NYC, San Van Party Pack, and Time is Money Pack. They sit in dlc/ beside skate3.exe, which is where the README says to put them. To add more, drop the package file in that same folder.

COMMAND-LINE: the exe accepts --game_data_root, --fullscreen, --window_width and --window_height if you ever want them as Steam launch options. None are set by default — the in-app settings persist in the portable folder, so they're the better place to configure it.
notes:
Built 2026-07-31. Source: github.com/mchughalex/skate3recomp. NOT an emulator and not a port — a static recompilation of the Xbox 360 binary; v2.0.0+ uses a native D3D12/Vulkan renderer rather than emulating the 360 GPU. Requires a user-supplied legally-obtained 360 ISO, which the app extracts once via its own GUI.

STAGED COPY IS ALREADY EXTRACTED. X:\_games\Skate 3\Skate3Recomp-Windows\ holds skate3.exe (96.9 MB), rexruntime.dll (17.8 MB), game/data/ with the extracted .big files (~5.95 GB) and dlc/ with four packs (652 MB) — 111 files, 6.71 GB total. A deploy lands a ready-to-run copy; the ISO step does not need repeating.

TWO COPIES EXIST, AND THE STAGED ONE IS NEWER. D:\Recompilations\Skate 3 Recompiled\ holds an older build (skate3.exe 94.4 MB, 2026-06-14) alongside the source ISO and the release zips; the staged copy is the 2026-07-25 build (96.9 MB). Only the DLC was taken from the D: copy. Its game/data also contains webkit/EAWebkit.xexp (4 KB) which the newer build's extraction does NOT produce — deliberately not carried over, since a recompilation has no use for an Xbox 360 executable patch and the newer extractor dropping it reads as intentional. Add it only if the in-game browser misbehaves. The four dlc .zip archives in the D: copy were skipped: each contains exactly the hash-named package already extracted beside it, so they are 563 MB of pure redundancy.

APPID PINNED to 3283182477, read out of _state/shortcuts/steamdeck.json where the existing shortcut points at Skate3Recomp-Linux/skate3. That appid also keys the captured artwork in _state/artwork/3283182477. Without the pin, steam_shortcut would derive crc32('gfm:skate-3')|0x80000000 = 3655991565 and add a SECOND entry — the same trap that caught gow2-hollow. Registry entry added alongside.

NESTED LAYOUT: the exe is one level down in Skate3Recomp-Windows/, so exe and start_dir are both relative to that, and marker_files matches it. Detection still resolves by folder name first ('Skate 3'), so it matches before the Windows build is deployed.

WATCH THE DISK: the device already has Skate3Recomp-Linux/ in Games/Skate 3/. Deploy adds files, it doesn't remove them, so after deploying you'll have BOTH builds — roughly 12 GB. Delete the Linux folder once the Windows build is confirmed good.

save_paths points at Skate3Recomp-Windows/saves, which is where portable mode should put user data — CONFIRM THE ACTUAL LAYOUT on first run (the README documents 'a saves folder next to the executable' but doesn't spell out where the settings file lands) and widen save_paths if the config sits elsewhere in that folder. Getting this right is what makes the Vulkan setting itself reimage-proof.

Known upstream issues (project README): texture/asset pop-in on fast traversal, skater customisation rendering, Hall of Meat rendering, skate park visual parity. UNTESTED as a recipe on hardware.
